transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Hannah Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (AuroraCloud Partnerships), Ethan Zhou (AuroraCloud Solutions Arch), Lara Gomez (AuroraCloud PM), Tom Becker (AuroraCloud Security)

Summary:
Quick sync to align Redwood reference architecture for AuroraCloud marketplace listing, review security/KMS flow, VPC options, and plan a small pilot. Action items captured at the end.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing requirements
- Reference architecture (hosted vs private vs hybrid)
- Networking: VPC peering, egress, private endpoints
- Security: KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC2 items
- Pilot scope and benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we figured we'd run through the reference arch and then dig into the security bits and then next steps for marketplace listing, sound good?
[00:15] Priya Nair: yep sounds good from our side, thanks Maya, we are trying to get the listing live by end of Q3 so want to make sure we understand the network and compliance reqs
[00:30] Daniel Ortiz: great, i'll share my screen in a sec, sorry my wifi is a bit spotty so if audio drops i will re-join
[00:45] Ethan Zhou: no problem daniel, quick context on our side — we run multi-tenant control plane but require private deployments for certain regulated customers, marketplace listing should support both hosted and a private package that we can deploy into customer VPC, ok?
[01:05] Hannah Lee: that's exactly the pattern we've seen — Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated pools and private (VPC/on-prem). for the RA diagram i want to confirm the private flow: customer VPC peering to redwood infra? or repo show that?
[01:22] Lara Gomez: yeah we have two flavors: marketplace "managed" offering (hosted) and a "bring your own infra" package (private) where marketplace just lists the package and then our infra team helps deploy.
[01:40] Daniel Ortiz: right, so the RA we've been drafting has three lanes: 1) Hosted - calls to Redwood public API with tenant isolation; 2) Dedicated - reserved GPU pools with customer-specific creds; 3) Private - control plane in AuroraCloud but data plane in customer's VPC. The private one is the one we want to clarify today.
[02:05] Tom Becker: security lead here — key question is where keys live. we require KMS integration and ideally customer-managed keys for private deployments. also audit logs must go to our SIEM, and network egress must be minimized.
[02:25] Maya Chen: absolutely, for private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integrations; the reference arch shows a KMS arrow from customer KMS to the data plane for token decryption, but let me, uh, point out — sometimes the diagram labeling gets fuzzy in exported docs so we'll update that.
[02:45] Priya Nair: i sometimes see the term "control plane" and "data plane" mixed up in other vendor docs, can we verbally confirm: control plane stays in AuroraCloud marketplace control plane, but the model serving (data plane) runs in customer VPC and stores KV caches locally?
[03:05] Daniel Ortiz: yes that's the intention. control plane in AuroraCloud/Redwood exchange for billing & management, data plane pinned to customer VPC so model weights and caches stay in private subnets. note: we do allow optional prefix caching to be cached at regional edge for latency sensitive flows, but that would require explicit egress rules.
[03:35] Ethan Zhou: okay that matches our compliance note. regarding marketplace listing metadata, our product team needs the package manifest to include allowed regions and whether KMS is optional or required.
[03:50] Lara Gomez: and also, do you have any constraints on network ports or need for a NAT gateway? we try to avoid forcing customers to open broad egress.
[04:05] Hannah Lee: good question — the private data plane only needs outbound TLS to Redwood control plane endpoints and to your internal artifact store if pulling images. we can support a private endpoint model (no public IP) but then there are implications for metrics/observability — we can stream logs to your SIEM over a secure path.
[04:30] Tom Becker: when you say "stream logs" is that push or pull? we normally require push over TLS to a collector in our security VPC.
[04:42] Daniel Ortiz: push — Redwood agents can push audit logs and token-level traces to a customer collector; we'll include schema and sample queries in the RA doc.
[04:04] Maya Chen: i'll note that as an action. moving on, benchmarking — Priya you mentioned QPS targets earlier, can you share ballpark numbers so we size GPU pools?
[05:15] Priya Nair: for the customers we're aiming at, peak can be 600 rps per region for small inc instances but typically bursts to 1.2k. many also want 99th percentile latency under 400ms for short completions.
[05:35] Daniel Ortiz: that helps. for the marketplace managed offering we'd recommend autoscaling dedicated pools; for private we can define a recommended GPU profile and candidate models for quantized inference to hit that latency. i'll propose two model variants in the pilot.
[05:55] Ethan Zhou: pilot — yes, we want a small pilot where you run two models: a high-accuracy and a quantized low-latency. measure cost per token and 95/99 latency.
[06:12] Maya Chen: exactly. daniel will draft a mini-benchmark plan. daniel, can you speak briefly about kernel & quantization support — any caveats with our infra?
[06:30] Daniel Ortiz: sure, so Redwood's runtime picks kernel paths based on architecture and sequence length. quantized models require a slightly different memory layout; for NVIDIA A100 we have optimized kernels; if AuroraCloud uses newer Arm-based instances we do have experimental kernels but would want to run smoke tests. so we should capture the instance SKU list for pilot.
[06:58] Lara Gomez: AuroraCloud currently offers m6g-like arm SKUs in a few regions, and x86 in others — i'll include the SKU list.
[07:10] Ethan Zhou: regarding marketplace listing copy, we need clear language around what the buyer gets: "Hosted offering" versus "Private package (customer-managed keys)" — any sample text?
[07:25] Maya Chen: we have boilerplate we can share; i'll add a marketplace blurb and the RA diagram to the shared drive. link: https://redwood.example.com/ra/auroracloud-draft (placeholder)
[07:40] Priya Nair: perfect. on compliance — Tom, any more specifics beyond KMS and log push?
[07:50] Tom Becker: SOC2 attestation is mandatory for the marketplace listing, and we also want TLS across all internal service boundaries, RBAC for operators, and a clear data retention policy.
[08:05] Hannah Lee: Redwood can provide SOC2 report and an export of our RBAC model; data retention is configurable per deployment. we'll attach the compliance pack link after call.
[08:20] Daniel Ortiz: small note — sometimes transcripts have names like KV cache spelled K-V cache or K V cache in docs; just flagging because the RA diagram text can get parsed in the marketplace portal.
[08:35] Lara Gomez: haha yes the portal parser is picky. please make sure the manifest uses the exact keys we require: "kms_required": true/false, "regions": [..], "privacy_level": "private|managed" — we'll share the manifest schema.
[08:55] Maya Chen: we'll align. quick question from my side — are there any legal procurement steps that block listing? Priya?
[09:05] Priya Nair: procurement requires a marketplace seller agreement and a security questionnaire; we can expedite once we have the SOC2 and RA doc, otherwise review takes weeks.
[09:18] Maya Chen: ok thanks. we'll put SOC2 link in the packet.
[09:25] Ethan Zhou: on the technical side, one thing to watch — model weight artifacts may be large, so image pulls in private VPCs need bandwidth planning; do you have a recommended approach?
[09:38] Daniel Ortiz: common pattern: use an artifact cache in the region or pre-warm images during deploy window; for very large models we recommend using quantized variants for private deployments to reduce transfer times.
[09:55] Lara Gomez: noted. about billing — do you support marketplace metering integration?
[10:05] Hannah Lee: yes we have metering hooks that can emit usage events compatible with AuroraCloud's marketplace billing API; we'll include a sample webhook in the RA doc.
[10:20] Priya Nair: great. next, the pilot timeline — we want to start infra smoke tests in two regions in July if possible.
[10:30] Maya Chen: doable — schedule wise we'll need 2 weeks to provision private data plane and run smoke tests. daniel will propose dates.
[10:40] Daniel Ortiz: i'll prepare the provisioning checklist, including instance SKUs, VPC peering steps, required ports, and service accounts.
[10:50] Tom Becker: for the service accounts we require least privilege and the keys rotate automatically; also we want to validate that audit logs can't be tampered with.
[11:05] Daniel Ortiz: understood — we'll set up signed logs with push to your collector and include a small tamper-evidence proof-of-concept.
[11:20] Maya Chen: ok we're at about 50 minutes, let's recap next steps.
[11:25] Priya Nair: recap from my side: updated RA, SOC2, manifest schema, SKU list, pilot dates.
[11:30] Maya Chen: good. action items — daniel, benchmark plan; maya, share RA & marketplace blurb; eth an, provide QPS/SKU list; priya, share manifest schema; tom, confirm security checklist. we'll schedule follow-up for pilot kickoff.
[11:50] Ethan Zhou: one more quick misc note — we may want a joint solution blurb for marketing once pilot passes, but that's after launch.
[11:58] Maya Chen: great, thanks everyone. we'll email the packet and loop infra owners.
[12:05] Priya Nair: thanks all, bye.
